answer: I would like to describe a lovely afternoon I spent with my nephew. Not long ago, during the winter, my elder sister paid us a surprise visit from Dhaka with her four-year-old son, and I ended up spending a whole afternoon with him. My sister had some errands to run in town with my mother, so I happily volunteered to keep him entertained. I had always found him endearing, but this was the first time we had really had a proper day together, just the two of us. He was remarkably [[inquisitive]] for his age, firing off questions about almost everything, some of which genuinely stumped me, like why the river never runs out of water. We built a fort out of cushions, drew a few clumsy animals, and I read him a couple of stories, putting on silly voices that he found hilarious. Later we walked down to the bank of the Jamuna to watch the boats, which he absolutely loved. What struck me most was how [[perceptive]] children are: he picked up on my mood instantly and kept trying to cheer me up. By evening I was exhausted, but it was the most [[rewarding]] kind of tiredness. It reminded me that spending time with a child forces you to slow down and be fully present, something adults rarely manage. Honestly, that afternoon was [[a welcome escape]] from my usual routine, and I have made a point of seeing him more often since, even if that means a long bus journey to Dhaka.

followUps.q: Do you enjoy spending time with children in general?
followUps.answer: Yes, I do, although I find it quite tiring. Children are so honest and [[unfiltered]] that you cannot pretend around them, and I think that is rather refreshing compared with the adult world.

followUps.q: Would you like to have children of your own one day?
followUps.answer: I think so, but not for a few years. I would like to be settled in my career first, and perhaps finish studying abroad, so that I can give them proper time and attention.

note: Added why I looked after him (errands), a walk by the Jamuna and a closing line; moved plain mark 'escape' to the phrase 'a welcome escape'.
